transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (Head of ML - Sparrow Tech), Rajiv Menon (Infra Lead), Tom Bennett (Finance), Jia Li (Product)

Summary:
Sparrow Tech is evaluating Redwood for an initial pilot (customer support & search augmentation). Main focus: per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private best fits their budget and compliance needs. They are cost-sensitive with a hard budget ceiling for Q2 pilot. Action items and pilot next steps agreed.

Topics covered:
- Current inference stack and token mix
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs (batching / KV caching / quantization)
- Hosting fit: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs VPC/Private
- Compliance/residency questions and KMS integration
- Pilot scope and pricing scenarios

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros — I'm Maya from Redwood, and Carlos our SE is here. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ellen (Sparrow): Hi, Ellen here. We're excited — we just want to make sure this pilot doesn't explode the budget.
[00:10] Tom (Finance): Hi, Tom — yes, budget is the headline. We have a fixed pilot cap of about $12k for compute.
[00:15] Carlos (SE): Great, thanks. We'll focus on unit econ and deployment fit. Can you talk through the token mix? Average prompt lengths, expected calls per second?
[00:23] Ellen: Sure, our baseline is a lot of short completions — average 60-120 input tokens, outputs around 40 tokens, but we also have a long form assist that can go to 800 tokens at lower frequency. Peak qps around 5-8 for the pilot, steady-state 1-2.
[00:36] Rajiv (Infra): Important note — data residency for some EU customers, but pilot data's fine in US. We will need KMS + audit logs if we move to private later.
[00:43] Maya: OK good. On cost levers — the three main ones are batching, KV/prefix caching for repeat prompts, and model/quantization choices. For Hosted we have per-token pricing; Dedicated gives better predictable per-token effective cost at scale via reserved GPU pools; Private is more heavy lift and license+support.
[00:58] Ellen: Real question: can you show a scenario where we stay under $12k with our mix? We want a concrete per-call cost.
[01:05] Maya: Yes, simplest is to sketch two scenarios: hosted with aggressive batching and caching, and dedicated with reserved capacity and quantized model. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[01:12] Carlos: Quick math on the call — if your average call is 100 tokens consumed (in+out) and we assume Hosted price of $0.0006 per token (example tier), that's $0.06 per call, so 200k calls would be $12k. But batching can reduce effective tokens billed and dual caching can reduce repeated context costs.
[01:29] Tom: That $0.0006 number — is that the actual Redwood published rate? We're hunting for realistic numbers not marketing.
[01:34] Maya: That's an illustrative number to show there are levers. Real pilot pricing will be in the spreadsheet. Also Dedicated at reserved utilization can drop unit cost by roughly 30-50% depending on batch sizing and sequence length.
[01:45] Jia (Product): Can you explain how KV cache helps? We have many repeated prompts across similar users.
[01:49] Carlos: Sure — KV caching stores transformer key/value states for repeated prefixes so subsequent calls with the same context reuse those cached tokens, drastically reducing per-call compute for continuation scenarios. In practice it looks like 20-60% savings if traffic has high repeat prefix locality.
[02:03] Ellen: Our main assist flow reuses the first 4-6 turns a lot, so sounds promising. Any risks for consistency or hallucination with caching?
[02:10] Carlos: No model semantics change; caching only avoids recomputing those keys. But you have to be careful with dynamic personalization — old cache entries might not reflect updated user state. We recommend TTLs and cache invalidation hooks.
[02:21] Unknown (Speaker 1): (muffled) how about quant... quantization?
[02:25] Maya: Yes, quantization is another lever. 8-bit quant vs FP16 can reduce memory & cost but may slightly affect quality for some models. Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles per workload.
[02:35] Rajiv: From infra side, we prefer Dedicated if we need consistent latency and large KV caches because we can allocate GPU pools. But procurement needs to see the math.
[02:44] Tom: Procurement will also ask about SLAs and escalation paths — what uptime / latency guarantees do you offer with Dedicated?
[02:50] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA summary in the pack. For Hosted we have operational SLOs but Dedicated is what we sell for predictability.
[02:59] Ellen: Security — can you integrate with our KMS for keys? We can't expose keys to third-party if we go Private later.
[03:05] Carlos: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS and provide audit logs. Hosted is more limited but we do support encryption-at-rest and standard SOC2 controls. We'll share the security brief.
[03:18] Jia: One thing: our product team worries about cold starts and latency spikes during peak. How does batching affect tail latency?
[03:25] Carlos: Batching increases throughput but can add queuing latency; Redwood's runtime supports latency SLOs with continuous batching thresholds. You can set policies — e.g. max batch wait 50 ms — and the runtime will prioritize lower-latency pools. Also we recommend a hybrid routing policy: high-priority traffic to low-latency dedicated pool, background tasks to batch-optimized pool.
[03:44] Tom: So hybrid hosting is possible? Mix Hosted + Dedicated?
[03:47] Maya: Yes hybrid routing is common. Smart routing will fall back to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, or route cost-sensitive jobs to quantized models.
[03:55] Rajiv: For the $12k cap, if we do a Dedicated reservation, any minimum commit? We can't sign a big annual until we see results.
[04:02] Maya: Dedicated often requires a monthly commit; we can do a short pilot-reserved capacity for a month to get predictable unit costs. There's also burst options. We'll model a one-month reserved vs pure hosted for the pilot.
[04:12] Ellen: Can you give an example where caching reduces cost on our repetition-heavy workloads?
[04:15] Carlos: Example: baseline call 100 tokens, 40 repeated tokens cached. Without caching you pay for 100 tokens; with caching you pay for 60 new tokens compute + minimal KV lookup cost. So effective token reduction 40%. If price is $0.0006/token, you save $0.024 per call. Over 200k calls that's ~$4.8k saved.
[04:35] Ellen: That's the kind of number we need.
[04:38] Jia: What about model choice? Would you recommend a smaller LLM for short completions?
[04:41] Carlos: Yes, model selection is another lever. For short, high-frequency tasks a smaller curated model might be sufficient and much cheaper. Redwood's catalog includes vetted models with performance profiles.
[04:52] Unknown (Speaker 1): (briefly) competitor pricing question — how does this compare to Anthropic / OpenAI?
[04:57] Maya: We don't want to get into line-by-line pricing comparisons on a call, but generally you can see similar per-token prices; our differentiation is predictable serving runtimes, caching, and deployment modes which change effective per-token economics. We'll include a comparison note.
[05:10] Tom: Procurement will also want to know about invoicing cadence and overage protections.
[05:13] Maya: For pilots we can invoice monthly; we can also set hard budget caps on API keys to prevent runaway spend.
[05:20] Rajiv: Operationally: if we route high-priority requests to Dedicated and backup to Hosted, how does data residency work? We can't send EU traffic to US-hosted during failover.
[05:29] Carlos: You can configure region-based policies. Fallbacks can be region-aware; if you require EU-only we can set failover to EU Dedicated or block cross-region fallback. We'll surface any policy constraints in the pilot doc.
[05:40] Ellen: Good. Next — can you walk through a pilot timeline?
[05:44] Maya: Typical pilot: week 0 onboard + test prompts, week 1 integration + small traffic, week 2 run baseline, week 3 fine tune caching/batching, week 4 review and decision. Given procurement cycles you might want an extra week for sign-off.
[05:58] Jia: We need to measure quality: latency, token cost, and a small set of golden prompts for regression.
[06:04] Carlos: We'll help define the eval set. Redwood Optimize can run quality monitoring and alert on regressions.
[06:10] Tom: Back to numbers — can you model a case: Hosted + caching vs Dedicated reserved for one month with 70% utilization?
[06:17] Carlos: We'll do that in the spreadsheet. We'll include assumed prices, utilization, batch sizes, and expected unit costs. We'll show sensitivity to average sequence length.
[06:25] Ellen: What's the onboarding effort for Private (VPC/on-prem)? We're not there for pilot but want to know ballpark days.
[06:32] Maya: Private is heavier — expect 4-8 weeks for VPC & HSM integrations typical. We can do Dedicated in days to weeks depending on network access.
[06:41] Rajiv: One more infra nit: KV cache size and eviction policies — on Dedicated can we pin cache to avoid eviction during peaks?
[06:48] Carlos: Yes, Dedicated pool sizing allows larger KV caches in memory. We can configure eviction + TTL and prioritize pins for hot prefixes.
[06:56] Ellen: I want to make sure we capture action items — can we review?
[06:59] Maya: Sure. Action 1: I'll send a pilot pricing spreadsheet showing Hosted vs Dedicated vs hybrid with batching/cache assumptions. Action 2: Carlos runs a quick sim. Action 3: Ellen shares sanitized sample prompts. Action 4: Tom clarifies budget cadence.
[07:14] Tom: I'll get the procurement window and confirm the $12k pilot cap is the right number and get back by Friday.
[07:19] Ellen: We'll try to have the sample prompts to you by Wednesday.
[07:21] Jia: Also schedule the technical deep-dive with Carlos next week.
[07:25] Maya: Great. We'll propose a 60m slot for Feb 19.
[07:29] Unknown (Speaker 1): (off-mic) thanks all.
[07:31] Maya: Anything else on risk? From Redwood side we also recommend a short eval of correctness on 50 golden prompts during week 2 to ensure quant/ smaller-model tradeoffs don't regress NPS.
[07:43] Carlos: Quick note on billing: our hosted metering sometimes rounds tokens; for pilot spreadsheets we'll show effective tokens and invoiced tokens differences.
[07:52] Rajiv: How do we instrument traces? We want per-request token and latency breakdowns for our dashboards.
[07:58] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and per-route dashboards; we can send screenshots.
[08:05] Ellen: Ok that helps. Any other blockers?
[08:09] Tom: None from finance beyond the cap and PO timing.
[08:12] Jia: We'll check internal legal for standard DPA, but for pilot we can use standard terms.
[08:16] Maya: We'll attach the security and SOC2 docs when I send the pack.
[08:20] Ellen: Perfect.
[08:22] Maya: Wrap up: we'll share the spreadsheet + security brief + proposed pilot schedule by Feb 12, schedule the SE deep-dive for Feb 19, and Carlos will run the latency sim by Feb 16.
[08:33] Carlos: One more micro example I want to email — a sample batching config that uses 50ms max latency and dynamic batch sizing. I'll include that in the doc.
[08:41] Ellen: Great, thanks.
[08:43] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.

End of transcript.
